interpretations: Use each rating’s average of nonmissing film lengths. Compute a baseline from all films with nonmissing lengths, counting each film equally. Keep ratings above the baseline, then keep only those above the equally weighted mean of the first set of ratings’ averages. Return the equally weighted mean of the final ratings’ averages, their mean excess over the baseline, and their mean excess over the first set’s mean.

Use the same baseline and filtering steps. Return the equally weighted mean of the final ratings’ averages, their mean excess over the baseline, and their mean excess over the final ratings’ own mean.
queries:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length
  FROM film
  WHERE length IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rating
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length
  FROM film
  WHERE length IS NOT NULL
),
first_set AS (
  SELECT r.rating, r.avg_length
  FROM rating_averages AS r
  CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
  WHERE r.avg_length > b.avg_length
),
first_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_length
  FROM first_set
),
final_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_length
  FROM first_set
  WHERE avg_length > (SELECT avg_length FROM first_mean)
)
SELECT
  f.avg_length AS mean_rating_length,
  f.avg_length - b.avg_length AS mean_excess_over_baseline,
  f.avg_length - m.avg_length AS mean_excess_over_first_set
FROM final_mean AS f
CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m
